h1: A growth consultant for roofing companies that want steadier months
intro: A storm comes through and the phone will not stop. Two months later it is quiet, and you are wondering how to make payroll. Meanwhile, estimates sit in someone's truck for a week before anyone follows up. A growth consultant for roofing companies helps you smooth out those swings and win more of the jobs you already bid.
definition: A growth consultant for roofing companies is an outside advisor who works with the owner on getting found, handling leads and estimates, connecting the tools you use, and making the key decisions on hiring and numbers.

paras: Roofing has its own set of headaches. These are the ones I see most.
bullets: Storm-driven swings: too much work after hail or wind, then not enough.
Slow follow-up on estimates: quotes go out, then nobody calls back.
Mixed leads: commercial and residential jobs coming in through the same door and handled the same way.
Hiring sales reps: not sure who to hire, how to pay them or how to tell if they are working.
Estimating tools: software that is paid for but half used, or that does not talk to your CRM.

sections.h2: How a growth consultant for roofing companies helps
paras: First I find the bottleneck. More leads on a broken process only means more lost estimates and longer nights. So in the first week we agree on the one pressure point that matters most, then fix it with your team.

For many roofers that starts with the sales process: who answers the call, who runs the inspection, how fast the estimate goes out, and who follows up and when. Small fixes here often show up quickly in signed jobs.

Storm work finds you. Steady work has to be earned. I build or rebuild your website and do ongoing SEO and AEO so you show up on Google, Google Maps and in AI answers from ChatGPT and Gemini for repairs, replacements, inspections and commercial work, not just after a storm. No one can guarantee rankings, but steady work on the basics gives you a fair shot.
I connect the tools you already use, like your CRM, estimating software, phones and forms, so leads and estimates do not fall through the cracks. I do not sell software.

In four 30-minute owner sessions a month, we work on the decisions in front of you: when to hire a sales rep, how to split commercial and residential, and which numbers to watch each week. Contracts, entity questions and taxes go to your attorney or CPA.

I am based in Charlotte, NC, and work with roofing companies locally and across the US, including a commercial roofer on the West Coast. Before this, I spent over a decade in banking and finance working with owners through cash crunches, then co-founded a company myself. Partnerships start at $3,000 a month for 90 days, then month to month.

faq.q: What does a growth consultant for roofing companies do?
faq.a: A growth consultant helps a roofing owner get more of the right leads and win more of the jobs they bid. That usually means work on your website and Google presence, a review of how leads and estimates are handled, connecting your tools, and regular sessions on decisions like hiring and pricing.

faq.q: How do I get more roofing leads outside of storm season?
faq.a: Build steady demand for work that is not storm driven, like repairs, maintenance, inspections and commercial jobs. A strong Google Business Profile, a page for each service, steady reviews and fast follow-up all help. Paid ads can add volume, but they work best once your sales process is solid.

faq.q: How fast should a roofing company follow up on an estimate?
faq.a: Follow up within a day or two, then on a set schedule until you get a yes or no. Many estimates are lost because nobody calls back, not because of price. A simple follow-up routine, tracked in your CRM, makes sure every estimate gets the same attention.

faq.q: When should a roofing company hire its first sales rep?
faq.a: Hire a sales rep when the owner is the bottleneck on inspections and estimates and good leads are waiting. Before hiring, write down your sales process so the rep has something to follow. Decide how you will pay them and which numbers you will track. Employment contracts go to your attorney.

faq.q: Should I handle commercial and residential roofing leads differently?
faq.a: Yes, in most cases. Commercial jobs usually involve longer sales cycles, more decision makers and bigger bids. Residential jobs often move faster and depend on trust and speed. Tracking them separately in your CRM, with their own follow-up steps, makes it easier to see which side is working.

faq.q: What does it cost to work with a roofing growth consultant?
faq.a: With Vestis, partnerships start at $3,000 a month for the first 90 days, then continue month to month. That covers a website build or rebuild, ongoing SEO and AEO, a sales process review, four owner sessions a month and support between calls. Paid ads are optional and extra.
